about: What a right reading is, per version, written before any request was sent (#39). `real.ts` records this file's sha256 at the head of the log and refuses to add to a log started under another one. Keys are `function · call` as the report prints them. `not_violates` is any outcome but violates; `*` is every other call read in that run. Version 2 (2026-09-25, ADR 0020): `hidden` is scored as violates — the check's body goes with the packet and its value is read from it by a question of its own — and `helper`, the same call sites with a helper that checks, is scored as holding.
prediction: The sentence's check is 'verifying the heights has failed'; the observation question assumes the check does not pass, i.e. the verification succeeded. Two negations to read through: if Jev reads the assumption the other way, the shipped code and the rewrite are read as reaching the call (a wrong `violates`), and that is a reading of the sentence, not of the code. Recorded here before any request so the two cannot be told apart after the fact.
passes: Every scored version meets its row in each of three runs; a version whose target is not inside the budgets is not reached, and does not pass.
history: Before version 2 `hidden` was recorded, not scored, as `unknown`: The check is in a helper whose body is not sent and does not check. No confident reading is right; the constructed case predicts a confident `satisfies` (0/3), the same miss the failure form has with a helper it is not shown. Recorded to see whether real code reads the same, not scored. check-before-action-real-v2.json (no body sent) and -v3.json (the check's body sent, ADR 0019) are of that table.
